subject: Technical deep dive: latency & throughput SLOs for Nimbus deployment
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Nimbus latency/throughput goals + next steps

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same context.

Summary of pain points you mentioned:
- Customer-facing search & summarization features are experiencing inconsistent latency during peak traffic windows (spikes up to ~1.2s for short queries).
- Costs have spiked as you scale generative features — want predictable unit economics for steady growth.
- Need a deployment topology that keeps PII inside your VPC and meets SOC2 readiness for audits.

Goals we heard:
- 95th-percentile latency target: <= 150ms for short prompts (~<=256 tokens) under normal load; acceptable burst latencies to 300ms with graceful degradation.
- Sustained throughput target: 350-400 QPS for text-generation endpoint (mixed prompt lengths, 30% long requests).
- Support for model family similar to Llama2-13B (quantized) with a fallback to a smaller 7B variant for cost-sensitive tiers.
- Private deployment (VPC) with KMS integration and audit logs.

Technical constraints you flagged:
- Max request size currently ~4k tokens in product; typical usage is 80-350 tokens.
- On-prem GPU preference: we heard you currently use NVIDIA A100; you may consider moving some capacity to cloud GPUs for burst.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Marissa to share a short technical note with suggested deployment topology (dedicated pool + autoscale policy + fallback model) and SLO calculations.
2) Acme to share a representative traffic sample (1 week) and a redacted prompt set for benchmarking.
3) Redwood to run a quick perf test with a quantized 13B variant and report expected cost per 1M tokens and achievable P95 latency.
4) Aditya/Marissa to put together an initial SLA/draft pricing addendum for review.

Attachments I’m including: redwood_sla_draft.pdf (draft terms) — we will refine after technical validation.

If this looks right, please confirm and share the sample traffic + prompts (link or S3) and we’ll prioritize the perf run this week.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Nimbus latency/throughput goals + next steps

Thanks Aditya — this is a very helpful summary. Confirming a few details and a couple of clarifying Qs: 

1) The P95 target of <=150ms is our ideal for interactive UX (search & inline summarize). For background batch jobs we expect higher latency and that’s OK.
2) Throughput target: the 350-400 QPS is what we need for peak marketing campaigns — average daily is closer to 80-120 QPS.
3) On model variants: yes, Llama2-13B quantized sounds like the right baseline. Fallback 7B for lower-cost endpoints is preferred.

Questions:
- Can Redwood provide an expected P95 at our peak mix (30% long requests)? A simple estimate would help us scope compute.
- For private deployments, is the KMS integration customer-managed keys (BYOK) or Redwood-managed? We need BYOK for compliance.

I’ll upload a redacted week of traffic and the prompt set to the shared folder you noted by EOD. Priya and I will review the SLA draft and propose minor redlines.

—Sam
VP Product, Acme Corp

Subject: Technical deep-dive: suggested topology & SLO calc for Acme Nimbus use-case

Hi Sam/Priya — following Aditya’s recap, I put together a short technical recommendation and some ballpark SLO calculations based on the targets you gave. Attaching topology diagram and a small SLO calc.

High-level recommendation (private VPC deployment):
- Deployment: Redwood Private in customer VPC with a dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity) in us-west1 for baseline traffic and cloud-bursting capability to GCP/Azure for marketing spikes.
- Model routing: Primary: quantized Llama2-13B (int8/4) on A100 80GB (or equivalent). Fallback: Llama2-7B quantized on smaller nodes for cost tiering.
- Autoscale policy: keep N baseline replicas to meet 80 QPS baseline; scale up replicas linearly to target 400 QPS with 60s cooldown; apply fast-path routing for short prompts to warm KV cache instances.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for popular prompts; token-level cache to reduce repeated decoding cost.
- Graceful degradation: implement tail-latency routing — when latency climbs above 200ms for >2min, automatically shift a % of requests to the 7B fallback.
- Security: BYOK KMS integration (customer-managed keys) + audit logs forwarded to your SIEM; private endpoint inside your VPC with mTLS to our control plane.

SLO / perf estimate (ballpark, needs validation with your traffic):
- Test assumptions: mix = 70% short (<256 tokens avg 120 tokens), 30% long (>=512 tokens avg 900 tokens); quantized 13B, A100 80GB, optimized kernels, batching disabled for latency-critical path but with micro-batching (up to 8) when latency headroom exists.
- Expected P95 latency:
  - Short requests: 90-140ms P95 depending on warmed KV cache (target achievable ~110ms)
  - Long requests: 300-600ms P95 depending on seq length
- Throughput: a dedicated pool of 8 A100s with concurrent streams configured should sustain ~360-420 QPS for the mixed workload above (depends on model optimization & quantization).
- Cost: rough estimate ~ $X per 1M tokens on 13B quantized baseline (we will provide exact numbers after a perf run).

Attached: nimbus_topology.png (topology + routing flow), slo_calc.xlsx (simple SLO calc), redwood_sla_draft.pdf (copied from Aditya).

Requested artifacts from Acme:
- Representative 1-week traffic sample (timestamps + token counts + endpoint) or a synthetic sample with comparable distribution.
- Redacted prompt set and a list of 10-20, high-value prompt templates.

Planned validation steps (what Redwood will do next):
1) Run a constrained perf test with your sample (quantized 13B) to measure P50/P95/P99 and per-token cost.
2) Provide updated SLO calculations and a recommended reserved capacity configuration (N baseline + autoscale thresholds).
3) Draft an SLA/pricing addendum tailored to the validated numbers.

If that all looks good I’ll schedule the perf run and loop in infra owners for BYOK setup.

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick call if you want to walk through the topology diagram.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
